Triage: `domain:cli` unchanged (`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`); **type `Bug`, `priority:p3`, `pm:queue`.** Half-state healed — lane without a pm-state.

## Grading

**In class, and on the user-facing side of the line.** This is not internal prose: `renderPnpmWorkspaceYaml()` output **ships into every project `objectstack init` scaffolds**, on the first screen of a file whose entire purpose is to be trustworthy about why each suppression exists. The paragraph explains a rule that **is not in the file it annotates**, and the card measures three separate falsehoods rather than asserting drift:

1. the `'@better-auth/scim>better-call'` entry retired with #3653, and `init.test.ts` **pins its absence**;
2. `@better-auth/scim` is not "held at a release candidate deliberately" — the family is pinned at exact stable `1.7.2`;
3. stable `@better-auth/scim@1.7.2` peers `better-call@1.4.0`, so the skew described does not exist.

⇒ Wrong, not incomplete. Documentation is inside class (a) when it is wrong, and a scaffold comment is documentation the user receives as an artifact.

## ⭐ The structural half — why no gate will ever catch this

`scaffold-workspace-consistency.test.ts` compares the rendered `allowedVersions` **map only**, and says so **on purpose**: *"The prose above each block is NOT compared: the two files explain these skews in their own words on purpose."*

⇒ The exemption is deliberate and defensible, and it means comment drift here is **structurally invisible**. ⛔ Do not "fix" this by making the tests compare prose — that would defeat the stated reason the two files word it differently, and it is not what this card asks for. Correct the paragraph.

`priority:p3`: nothing breaks, nothing resolves differently, no gate reddens. A scaffolded user reads a paragraph about a rule their file does not contain. Small, real, one-paragraph fix.

On today's tree `init.ts` says **1.7.3** at `:178` and **1.7.1** at `:142` and `:197` — the file **disagrees with itself**. ⇒ measure what the pinned version actually is on this tree (and what it peers) and use that; ⛔ do not carry 1.7.2, 1.7.1 or 1.7.3 forward on anyone's word, this seat's included. If the file's own two answers cannot both be right, say so — that is a finding worth its own line in the PR body.

⛔ So: do **not** widen `scaffold-workspace-consistency.test.ts`, `init.test.ts` or `create-objectstack`'s `template-consistency.test.ts` to compare comments. The deliverable is the corrected paragraph.

⭐ The sibling producer already models the wording: `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/pnpm-workspace.yaml` records the retirement in its own words. Read it and mirror the *shape*, ⛔ not necessarily the text — and re-measure its version claims too, since they may carry the same staleness.

## Red lines

- ⛔ **凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位，不论谁需要它** — `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:231` · `references/core-rules.md:62` · `SKILL.md:287` · `references/lanes/cli.md:12` · `references/lanes/spec.md:12` · `references/dispatch-runbook.md:158`. A `packages/spec` **edit** ⇒ stop and report. Reading is free.
- ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- 🔒 Open PRs holding lane files right now: **#17725** (`packages/cli/src/commands/{dev,serve}.ts`, `src/utils/dev-tls-contract.ts`, `plugin-hono-server/*`) and **#17718** (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`, `packages/verify/src/handle.ts`). Your face — `commands/init.ts` and, if you touch it, the `create-objectstack` template — is disjoint from both. If the delivered diff grows into either set, stop and say so.
- ⚠️ Re-derive `Clause-②` from the DELIVERED diff. Declared `no` because a rendered comment string moves no accept set and publishes no surface. If your diff moves a declaration rather than prose, say so — ⛔ never re-declare silently.

## Acceptance

1. **The corrected paragraph**, with each of the card's three claims re-stated against *your* measurement of today's tree (the entry is absent; the pin is not a release candidate; the peered version). Quote the bytes you measured.
2. **A rendered-output reading**, before and after: drive `renderPnpmWorkspaceYaml()` and show the paragraph as a scaffolded user receives it. ⛔ Not a source diff alone — the defect is in what ships.
3. **State what holds it** — given triage's boundary, probably nothing does. Say that plainly rather than inventing a gate; a named, accepted gap is a better deliverable than a gate that defeats a deliberate exemption.

⚠️ Every zero needs a **positive control from the SAME file**; a control borrowed from another artefact can only return 0. ⛔ A count is not a reading — this file discusses `better-call` in both a source docblock and a rendered string, and they say different things, so read every hit in context.

## Gates

The repo's fast checks **plus `pnpm lint`** (the lane always adds it; `dispatch-gates.mjs` does not name it). Heavy verification through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` — ⛔ different build chains do NOT avoid the queue, one lock per container. Changeset required unless the measurement shows nothing published moves, in which case say why. Open the PR as a **draft** with `Fixes #17093`.

Controls from these artefacts and able to fail: `peerDependencyRules` = **2**, the other live entry `@better-auth/scim>@better-auth/utils` = **1**, fabricated `scaffoldRetirementXYZZY` = **0**.

**The declarations did not move**: the diff on `init.ts` carries **no** added or removed `'x>y':` entry line. ⇒ the rendered `allowedVersions` map is unchanged; only prose moved, which is exactly what triage's boundary required.

### ⛔ A FOURTH instrument fault, mine, and a new shape

The first pass returned **0** on four of five claims — on text I had already read. The sibling template's two claims passed **under the same normaliser**, which is what located the fault: it was not the matcher, it was the *file*.

⭐ **The rendered block is a JS ARRAY of string literals, so a phrase that spans two literals picks up the array's `,` between them.** 「…used to sit here is retired…」 is really `'…used to sit here is',` + `'#   retired. …'`, and after stripping quotes and `#` it normalises to 「…used to sit here is, retired…」 — one comma the pattern did not have. ⇒ **every pattern must lie INSIDE one literal.**

That is now four distinct instrument faults in two landings, each a different mechanism: normalising the pattern with a regex-aware normaliser; collapsing whitespace before stripping markers; inferring an assertion's input from its shape; and now spanning a literal boundary. ⭐ The common remedy is the same one each time — **when a control passes and the claim does not, suspect the instrument before the artefact**, and go read the bytes.

### The risk the dev found on its own — confirmed

The corrected note contains the literal `'@better-auth/scim>better-call'`, which `init.test.ts:348` asserts is **absent**. It is not a contradiction: `settings` is defined at `:138`/`:264`/`:323` as `renderPnpmWorkspaceYaml().replace(/^\s*#.*$/gm, '')` — **comment-stripped**. The dev identified this as the one non-obvious risk and **measured** it (raw rendered 1, comment-stripped 0, control declaration 1) rather than assuming. ⛔ A reviewer who read only the assertion would have filed a defect that does not exist.

### One item carried forward, ⛔ not filed

`pnpm-workspace.yaml:107`-`:109` carries the same staleness one layer out — it says 「measured unchanged on 1.7.2, the version this lockfile now holds」 while `:239` pins `1.7.3`. ⚠️ Repo infrastructure, not a scaffold artefact, and nothing a user receives ⇒ ⛔ not a card-taking class. Successor: whoever next re-measures the better-auth family pins.
